The Airfoil GAN model is built upon the VAEGAN architecture, which combines the Variational Autoencoder (VAE) and Generative Adversarial Network (GAN) approaches.
The model encodes 200-dimensional airfoil coordinates into a 32-dimensional latent feature space.
K-means clustering in the learned feature domain shows that the feature vectors encode essential shape information without predefined design parameters.
The paper demonstrates that the Airfoil GAN model can generate novel airfoils by either interpolating/extrapolating feature vectors or sampling from Gaussian noise.
Some of the generated airfoils show competitive or even better aerodynamic properties compared to the airfoils used for model training.
The paper combines the Airfoil GAN model with a genetic algorithm to optimize the generated airfoils towards desired aerodynamic properties.
The Airfoil GAN model is trained on the UIUC Airfoil Coordinates Database, which contains more than 1,600 2D airfoils.
The input airfoil coordinates are preprocessed by scaling the x-coordinates to [0, 1] and interpolating 100 points along the upper and lower boundaries.
The encoder and decoder components of the Airfoil GAN model are built using multi-layer perceptrons (MLPs).
The discriminator component of the Airfoil GAN model is also implemented using an MLP architecture.
The training of the Airfoil GAN model involves optimizing a combination of reconstruction loss, KL divergence loss, layer consistency loss, and adversarial loss.
The paper demonstrates that the Airfoil GAN model can effectively parameterize existing airfoil shapes and generate novel airfoils without relying on predefined design parameters.
The genetic algorithm used for aerodynamic optimization operates directly on the learned latent feature vectors of the Airfoil GAN model.

The paper shows that the Airfoil GAN approach can lead to the design of a new generation of airfoils that are more intelligent and efficient compared to those relying on experimental experience or manually selected design parameters.
The Airfoil GAN model is able to generate smooth airfoil shapes without any additional post-processing, unlike traditional parameterization methods that can produce irregular and wavy shapes.
